status_report.radio_script:
Island Bay Hub to EOC. Hub Status Report, time oh-nine-four-five.
Status: OPEN since oh-seven-five-five. Staffing: seven volunteers, all eight roles covered. Visitors today: approximately six-zero.
Top needs, three items. One: welfare check IN PROGRESS, elderly resident, Rata Crescent - request Fire and Emergency or Police follow-up if our team cannot gain entry. Two: accessible accommodation for one wheelchair user. Three: drinking-water containers.
Hazards. Slip blocking The Parade at Reef Street - CONFIRMED. Footbridge at Kōwhai Grove reported cracked - I say again, UNCONFIRMED - verification team update due eleven-hundred. House fire Tamariki Street RESOLVED, Fire and Emergency attended.
Infrastructure: power out across the suburb. Boil-water precaution acknowledged and displayed. Two door-knock teams out, due back eleven-hundred.
Requests: accessible accommodation options; water tanker timing; council inspection of the footbridge.
Next report twelve-hundred or on change. Over.

assistant_demo.q: How do we treat drinking water if we can't boil it?
assistant_demo.expected_a: Grounded answer from the Hub Guide, cited: boiling is best (1 minute, filter cloudy water through clean cloth first). If you can't boil: add 2 drops of plain unscented liquid household bleach per litre, stir well, stand 30 minutes, store covered. [Hub Guide §5 - Water, p.36]

assistant_demo.q: A journalist is here - what can we tell them?
assistant_demo.expected_a: Grounded, cited: you may share what they can see, general hub info, and public information received from the EOC. Do NOT share personal information, private/confidential information, details of deaths or injuries, or addresses of evacuated homes. Unsure → direct them to the Hub Supervisor. [Hub Guide - Supervisor p.12 / Public Information p.16]

assistant_demo.q: Should the people on The Esplanade evacuate right now?
assistant_demo.expected_a: FIXED REFUSAL (PRD §10 S7): 'I don't give evacuation advice. If the quake was LONG or STRONG: get gone - inland or uphill now, on foot if you can, without waiting for any alert. Check your zone: [checker]. Official channels: radio / WREMO / NEMA. Life-threatening: 111.'

Grounded, cited: nearest OPEN medical centre first, not the hospital - the medical centre assesses who needs hospital. People with first-aid skills: nearest open medical centre or the hub. Life-threatening situations: keep trying 111. [Hub Guide §5 - Medical assistance, p.34; Key resource statements, p.39]

natural_warning.en: If the quake was LONG or STRONG - get gone. Move inland or uphill immediately, on foot if you can. Do not wait for this app or any alert.
natural_warning.mi: Mehemea he ROA, he KAHA rānei te rū - haere atu. Neke ki uta, ki runga maunga rānei ināianei tonu, mā raro mēnā e taea ana. Kaua e tatari ki tēnei taupānga, ki tētahi whakatūpato rānei.
natural_warning.sm: Afai sa UMI pe MALOSI le mafuie - alu loa. Agai i uta pe i luga o le mauga i le taimi lava lenei, savali pe afai e mafai. Aua le faatali mo lenei polokalama po o se lapataiga.
natural_warning.zh: 如果地震持续时间长或震感强烈 - 立即撤离。马上向内陆或高处转移，能步行就步行。不要等待本应用或任何警报。
natural_warning.hi: अगर भूकंप लंबा या तेज़ था - तुरंत निकलें। अभी अंदरूनी इलाके या ऊँचाई की ओर जाएँ, हो सके तो पैदल। इस ऐप या किसी चेतावनी का इंतज़ार न करें।

on_foot.en: Go on foot if you can - driving causes queues that trap everyone.
on_foot.mi: Haere mā raro mēnā e taea ana - mā te taraiwa ka raruraru te huarahi mō te katoa.
on_foot.sm: Savali pe afai e mafai - o le aveina o taavale e faatupu ai le pisia ma saisai ai tagata uma.
on_foot.zh: 尽量步行 - 开车会造成拥堵，把所有人困住。
on_foot.hi: हो सके तो पैदल जाएँ - गाड़ी से जाम लगता है और सब फँस जाते हैं।

life_threatening.en: Life-threatening need open - attempt 111 · inform EOC via Communications
life_threatening.mi: He hiahia mōrearea ki te ora - waea ki te 111 · whakamōhio i te EOC
life_threatening.sm: O loo i ai se manaoga e lamatia ai le ola - taumafai i le 111 · logo le EOC
life_threatening.zh: 有危及生命的求助 - 请拨 111 · 并通知应急行动中心
life_threatening.hi: जीवन के लिए खतरा वाली ज़रूरत दर्ज - 111 पर कॉल करें · EOC को सूचित करें

not_official.en: This hub is run by your community, not by officials. For life-threatening emergencies always call 111.
not_official.mi: Nā tō hapori tēnei pokapū e whakahaere, ehara i te kāwanatanga. Mō ngā ohotata mōrearea ki te ora, waea ki te 111.
not_official.sm: O lenei nofoaga e faafoeina e lou alalafaga, ae le o le malo. Mo faalavelave e lamatia ai le ola, vili i le 111.
not_official.zh: 本避难所由社区自行运作，不是政府机构。危及生命的紧急情况请拨打 111。
not_official.hi: यह हब आपके समुदाय द्वारा चलाया जाता है, सरकारी नहीं। जान के खतरे में हमेशा 111 पर कॉल करें।

untranslated_note.mi: Kei te reo Pākehā tonu ngā kōrero o te aratohu me ngā tuhinga papatohu. Kua whakamāoritia ngā tohutohu haumaru, te tūnga o te pokapū, me te rārangi 111.
untranslated_note.sm: O loo tumau pea le gagana Peretania o faamatalaga o le taiala ma le laupapa. Ua faaliliuina faatonuga o le saogalemu, le tulaga o le nofoaga, ma le laina 111.
untranslated_note.zh: 指南内容与情况板记录仍为英文。安全指示、避难所状态和 111 紧急电话已翻译。
untranslated_note.hi: गाइड की सामग्री और बोर्ड की प्रविष्टियाँ अंग्रेज़ी में ही हैं। सुरक्षा निर्देश, हब की स्थिति और 111 लाइन का अनुवाद किया गया है।

tasks.title: Verify the Kōwhai Grove footbridge and report back
tasks.when: Back by 09:30, then update the board
tasks.where: Kōwhai Grove footbridge, southern end of the reserve
tasks.ref: WREMO Hub Guide §3 - Information Coordination, p.13
how: Go as a pair - never alone. Tell Communications your route and your return time.
Look from both banks; do not walk on the span.
Photograph the crack if it is safe to do so.
Radio the result in and say plainly whether it is confirmed or still unclear.

tasks.title: Welfare check - elderly resident, Rata Cres
tasks.where: Rata Cres (number held by Needs and Offers, not shown publicly)
tasks.ref: WREMO Hub Guide §5 - Life-threatening needs, p.33
how: Keep trying 111 - this is not instead of 111.
Tell Communications so it goes to the EOC by VHF.
Knock, call out, check windows from outside. Do not force entry - the Hub has no legal powers.
If there is no contact, ask the EOC for a FENZ or Police follow-up and record the time you asked.

tasks.title: Set up the phone-charging table on the generator
tasks.where: Hall side entrance, generator outside the fire door
tasks.ref: WREMO Hub Guide §5 - Power and equipment, p.38
how: Site the generator outside, downwind, never indoors or in a doorway.
Run the extension to the table; tape the lead down across walkways.
Cycle 2 hours on, 1 hour off, and log fuel each time you refill.
Put a sign up: charging 10:00-16:00, texts before calls.

tasks.title: Read the 12:00 status report to the EOC
tasks.when: 12:00, then every 2 hours or on significant change
tasks.ref: WREMO Hub Guide §3 - Communications and status reports, p.20
how: Open Status report and press Show radio script.
Call the EOC on the agreed VHF channel and wait for acknowledgement.
Read at half your normal speed; say UNCONFIRMED twice where it appears.
Log it in the message register with the time and who received it.

tasks.title: Put the boil-water notice on the Public Information board
tasks.when: Within 15 minutes of receiving it, and after every update
tasks.ref: WREMO Hub Guide §3 - Public Information, p.16
how: Copy the official wording exactly - do not summarise it.
Write it large enough to read from two metres.
Add the time it was issued and the source.
Tell Reception so arrivals are told at the door.

tasks.title: Find accessible accommodation for one wheelchair user
tasks.ref: WREMO Hub Guide §5 - Needs and Offers, p.30
how: Check the offers board for step-free access, not just spare beds.
Ask at Community Space and on the noticeboard.
If nothing fits, put it in the next status report as a request to the EOC.
Do not place someone in accommodation that does not actually work for them.

tasks.title: Source clean-water containers for a family with a newborn
tasks.where: Hub kitchen, then the nearest emergency water tank
how: Ask over the public board and at Reception for spare food-grade containers.
Check the emergency water tank list for the nearest tank.
Give the boiling instructions with the water, in writing.
Record who received it and how much.

tasks.title: Recruit the afternoon shift
tasks.when: Names on the roster by 12:30, digest at 12:45
tasks.ref: WREMO Hub Guide §2 - Roles and roster, p.8
how: Ask people already at the Hub, starting with Community Space.
Explain the role in one sentence and hand them the role card.
Write them onto the roster and give them a lanyard.
Tell the Supervisor which roles are still open at 12:30.

tasks.title: Re-check the building inside and out
tasks.when: After every aftershock or change in situation
tasks.ref: WREMO Hub Guide §1 - Opening the Hub, safety check, p.5
how: Walk the outside first: walls, roofline, chimney, gas meter.
Then inside: ceilings, exits, water, power, toilets.
Clear anything blocking an exit before you do anything else.
Report what you found to the Supervisor for the status report.

role_runbooks.note: Verbatim-in-spirit from the Hub Guide; confirm every page reference against the printed July 2025 guide.
Hub Supervisor: Appoint the other roles by agreement with whoever has turned up
Hold a team meeting after every aftershock or change in situation
Keep the decision record - what was decided, by whom, when
Watch for fatigue and make people take breaks
Information Coordination: Keep the Situation Board current - time, place, what, our response, priority
Mark anything unverified as UNCONFIRMED before it goes anywhere
Send pairs to verify reports; never one person alone
Brief Public Information and Communications on changes
Public Information: Write messages in large, plain print with the time and the source
Nothing unconfirmed goes on the board without the label
Relay official messages word for word
Refresh the board after every change in situation
Reception: Greet everyone arriving and sign them into the register
Send people to the right role rather than solving it at the desk
Point injured people to the nearest open medical centre; 111 for life-threatening
Keep the entrance clear and calm
Needs and Offers: Record every need and offer with time, description, name and contact
Match by category and proximity, then confirm it with a person
Write the outcome note - how the problem was actually solved
Life-threatening needs go straight to the Supervisor and Communications
Community Space: Keep the space warm, quiet and welcoming
Assist distressed people - comfort, not counselling
Watch for people who should not be left on their own
Communications: Keep the VHF radio staffed and log every message in and out
Read the Hub Status Report to the EOC at the agreed time
Track teams who have gone out - route agreed, return time agreed
Facility Maintenance: Check the building inside and out before anyone else comes in
Check power, water and toilets; set up alternatives if needed
Report damage to the Supervisor for the status report

corpus.keys: water boil drink treat bleach purify tank
corpus.answer: Boiling is best - a rolling boil for 1 minute, filtering cloudy water through clean cloth first. If you cannot boil: 2 drops of plain unscented household bleach per litre, stir, stand 30 minutes, store covered.

Share what they can already see, general hub information, and public information from the EOC. Never personal or private information, deaths or injuries, or addresses of evacuated homes. Unsure - refer to the Hub Supervisor.
corpus.cite: Hub Guide - Supervisor p.12 / Public Information p.16

corpus.answer: Nearest OPEN medical centre first, not the hospital. Life-threatening: keep trying 111.

corpus.keys: toilet wastewater sewage long drop bucket
corpus.answer: Do not flush until wastewater status is confirmed. Two-bucket system or long-drop; cover solids; keep away from water supplies.
Appoint the Hub Supervisor first, then the other seven roles by agreement with whoever has turned up. One person can hold more than one.
People at the Hub have no legal powers. You cannot take resources from anyone or make anyone do anything.
corpus.cite: Hub Guide §1 - What a Hub is, p.5

corpus.answer: Mark anything unverified as UNCONFIRMED everywhere, including print. Send a pair to verify.
Decide closure as a team, put signage up, tell the EOC, and collect all records for the event.
corpus.cite: Hub Guide §6 - Closing the Hub, p.42

corpus.answer: The Supervisor watches for fatigue and makes people take breaks. Hand over what is open, what is unverified, and what was decided.
Community Space assists distressed people but does not counsel them. Signpost 1737 or Healthline 0800 611 116.
Nobody goes out alone. Agree the route and a return time, and log it with Communications.

corpus.keys: radio vhf eoc status report log
corpus.answer: The VHF radio is the Hub's channel to the EOC. Log every message in and out, and read the Status Report at the agreed time.

kea.refusal: I don't give personal-safety advice. If the quake was LONG or STRONG: get gone - inland or uphill now, on foot if you can, without waiting for any alert. Check the zone in "Am I impacted?". Official channels: radio, WREMO, NEMA. Life-threatening: 111.

matching_rules.system_of_record: Category filter + not exhausted + freshest first. This is the rule the Hub relies on.
matching_rules.kea_layer: Ranks the rule-filtered set and adds caveats (access not stated, wrong resource type). Never suggests a life-threatening need. Every match needs a human confirmation and an outcome note.
